title: Algorithm Analysis and Big O
summary: How to compare algorithms independently of computers - counting basic steps, Big O notation and the common growth classes from O(1) to O(2^n), analysing loops, nested loops and halving, best, worst and average cases, the costs of Java's collection operations, measuring with System.nanoTime, and space complexity.

cards.q: What is the Big O of `5n² + 100n + 7`?
cards.a:
O(n²)

The fastest-growing term dominates and constant factors are dropped, so only `n²` is left.

cards.q: Why is a loop over `n` words that calls `contains` on an `ArrayList` inside it usually O(n²)?
cards.a:
`contains` scans the list, O(n), and it runs once per iteration of an O(n) loop

A method call costs what the method costs: an O(n) scan inside an O(n) loop multiplies to O(n²). A `HashSet` makes each `contains` O(1) on average.

cards.q: A loop does `for (int i = 1; i < n; i *= 2)`. How many times does it run?
cards.a:
about log₂ n

`i` doubles each time, so it reaches `n` after about log₂ n steps.

cards.q: Quicksort is O(n log n) on average. What is its worst case?
cards.a:
O(n²)

Quicksort can degrade to O(n²) when its pivots split the data badly; merge sort is the one that is O(n log n) always.
